Someone Paid Just $8,900 for a Tesla Model S, No Typo Here
13 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Gone are the days when the Tesla Model S was associated with deep-pocketed people, as the battery-electric sedan can now cost new (electric) bicycle money.
The average value tends to sit between $10,000 and over $100,000 for such a thing. It all depends on the model year, powertrain, mileage, and overall condition, and near-new trims, especially the neck-snappingly fast Plaid, can easily venture into the six-digit territor.
But this one is not a Plaid, nor a new model year example, as you are looking at a 2014 Tesla Model S 70. It has a clean California title, has never been crashed, and the odometer read 79,200 miles (~127,500 km) at the time of cataloging.
The known flaws category of the ad reveals that there are scuffs, dings, chips, and scratches on the outside, as well as a peeling finish on the left front door panel window switches, and creases and stains on the upholstery. Therefore, this EV has definitely seen a lot of usage. The tires carry 2020 and 2021 date codes, the listing shows.
According to the listing, which quotes the selling dealer, the battery capacity has increased to 70 kWh, and this, alongside the tinted windows, is the only notable modification.
Photo: Cars&Bids Power is supplied by a single electric motor, which is estimated to have produced 315 horsepower and 325 pound-feet (440 Nm) of torque or so when the car was new. The EPA-estimated driving range of this model was 234 miles (377 km) when it was still being sold.
This older Tesla Model S features a Red Multi-Coat exterior color on top of the tan interior. It rides on 21-inch Turbine wheels, has a 17-inch touchscreen display, piano black trim on the inside, power-adjustable seats at the front, rear-facing third-row seats, and a power sunroof.
In addition to the car, the new owner will get one key, and that is it. The vendor is a dealer that reportedly bought the electric sedan in June 2026, adding some 300 miles (~500 km) since. The selling price is not a surprise anymore, given that we mentioned it in the title, and just in case you missed it, here it is: $8,900.
The Tesla Model S in question was advertised at the excitement of no reserve on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction that ended on November 19, 2026. And we don’t know about you, but this is definitely a lot of car for the money, though it is something that not many people would have dared to buy. Are you one of them? Would you have bought this EV if you saw it advertised for $8,900? Tell us all about it in the comments area below, and then check out this ride in more detail here .

U.S. Army Soldiers with 3rd Battalion, 11th Field Artillery Regiment, 25th Infantry Division Artillery, conduct a fire mission rehearsal on an M777 howitzer during Lightning Surge 2 at Schofield Barracks, Hawaii, Feb. 20, 2026. The soldiers were testing a new workflow where fire missions, received digitally via the Next Generation Command and Control prototype, are executed at the gun line. This soldier-led feedback is helping the Army develop future capabilities that are more lethal, accurate, and effective. (U.S. Army photo by Lt. Col. Hayden Howell) (Depictions or descriptions of private industry personnel or products does not constitute endorsement or promotion by the U.S. Army or Department of War)
The Army’s Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) effort rests on a simple premise: the service can no longer afford C2 systems that can’t talk to one another, take years to update, or fail when an adversary jams a link. Those issues become particularly glaring when viewed in the light of operations across a theater as vast as the Indo-Pacific.
The Army’s answer is a shared data foundation with applications layered on top, replacing the separate, platform-specific systems that now serve fires, air defense, and logistics. Each piece is built so it can be swapped out while maintaining interoperability with the rest.
At its core, NGC2 is about “shifting the paradigm to a mission-centric operation,” said Chandra Marshall, vice president, programs, enterprise operations at Lockheed Martin . The Army wants a composable architecture with common applications and core services, she said, enabling integration of new software, weapons, and sensors without rework and knocking down silos at every echelon.
A threat picture that punishes stovepipes
The case for that shift starts with the electromagnetic spectrum. Josh Wallin, a defense program fellow at the Center for a New American Security, points to Ukraine, where Russian forces jam, interfere with, and track electromagnetic spectrum emissions. The US hasn’t faced an enemy that targets the spectrum so heavily, and the risk to communications and data links between Army forces grows against a capable adversary in the Indo-Pacific, he said.
Then there is geography. Neither the Global War on Terror, nor the current fight in Iran, nor even the war in Ukraine has required the Army to connect systems that might sit thousands of miles apart, Wallin said. Commercial infrastructure could fill some gaps, although relying on cellular networks would be more difficult. Satellite communications could offer another means of connectivity.
Bandwidth may prove the harder constraint. The Army, Navy, and Air Force are all pursuing distributed operating concepts, which assume scattered units will continually pass data among nodes to stay synchronized. With less massing of forces in a few locations, that data has to travel farther and over more contested paths.
Speed adds pressure, and in Ukraine, “we might be talking on the order of minutes from acquisition to servicing a target,” Wallin said.
The problem exists inside individual warfighting functions, too. For air defense, only recently have Patriot and THAAD been able to cue each other, with a THAAD radar controlling a Patriot interceptor. Layered defense can’t work if each system fights alone, Wallin argued. It’s “super inefficient,” he said, and against a large volume of incoming threats, stovepiped units may simply be unable to share information fast enough to coordinate a response.
Multinational partners pose for a photo after a counter-landing live-fire exercise as part of Exercise Balikatan 2026 at La Paz Sand Dunes, Laoag City, Philippines, May 4, 2026. (U.S. Army photo by Sgt. Duke Edwards)
The data layer is the foundation
The NGC2 data layer ingests information and makes it available to any application or operator according to role, access level, and warfighting function, Marshall explained. The Army sets the rules, and the system uses them to determine who needs a given piece of data and at what level of the force it should go.
This is a key challenge for NGC2 because air defense, logistics, and fires each run their own data and communications infrastructure. Centralizing data across them, according to Wallin, will give logisticians trying to sustain distributed forces visibility into ongoing operations, the threat picture, and intelligence feeds that once lived in separate systems.
Pooling the data is the first step. The next is drawing conclusions about how information across functions relate. The 25th Infantry Division in Hawaii has been the experimental unit charged with demonstrating the approach, with Lockheed Martin serving as the Full Stack Operational Implementation Lead.
During Lightning Surge 3 in April, the team fused sensors, fires systems, and airspace data into a single cloud-enabled picture, according to Marshall. She called it the first demonstration of cross-domain data sharing in the 25th ID environment, working across multiple locations that spanned Hawaii, the Philippines, and the broader Indo-Pacific. The outcome was a shared real-time view and compressed sensor-to-shooter timeline, she said.
The NGC2 program is also changing how the Army develops and fields C2 software. Rather than giving industry a fixed set of technical requirements, the Army established operational objectives that could be refined as soldiers used the systems. That has allowed developers to incorporate feedback directly from the field instead of waiting for the next major upgrade cycle.
“They give us feedback real time so we can make software changes within minutes, hours, days, depending on the complexity of the feature,” Marshall said. “When we conduct Lightning Surges, it’s about operational fight-tonight capability the 25th ID can use now. It’s not a prototype, so it’s been powerful in that regard.”
One example came during Lightning Surge 4, when soldiers wanted to operate the system without having to interact physically with a screen. Developers responded by integrating an AI-driven hand microphone with an Army edge device, allowing soldiers to issue spoken commands instead of touching. The capability was designed, built, and delivered within days, according to Marshall.
The approach represents a departure from programs in which requirements are established years before soldiers receive the resulting capabilities. Marshall said the team delivered NGC2 solutions in less than 10 months that the 25th ID used operationally across the Pacific and exercised during Balikatan, the annual US-Philippine military exercise.
AI as an aid, not a decider
Artificial intelligence (AI) is one of the applications layered on top of the data foundation, though both Marshall and Wallin were careful about how much weight to put on it. AI can comb through available data and turn it around to commanders quickly, cutting latency from minutes to seconds, according to Marshall. However, it is one tool among several, and it isn’t making decisions for the Army. It correlates data and offers recommendations so commanders have the right information at the right time. The decision aids already demonstrated are “very powerful,” she said.
The practical hope for AI, in Wallin’s view, is to automate what can be automated and speed up tasks that are heavily manual today. Even “a 60 percent solution on something that was 100 percent manual before” could free operators to focus on other responsibilities, he said.
Another important feature of NGC2 is that its architecture is designed so its layers can be pulled apart and replaced independently. The Army is trying to separate the physical data links, meaning which cable runs to which radio and which satellite, from the compute infrastructure, and to separate both from the software that manages the data, Wallin said. Soldiers interact with the application layers on top.
If an adversary finds a new way to jam or track something like a satellite terminal, the Army could replace that hardware with something less vulnerable without disturbing everything above it. Advances in computing power and the shrinking size of computing hardware could give the Army more room to accommodate future applications. More importantly, the service is moving away from the assumption that software and hardware acquired today must remain in service for decades.
The goal is to create an architecture that can continuously evolve as adversaries develop new methods of disrupting communications, targeting military networks, and exploiting vulnerabilities. Instead of replacing an entire C2 system, the Army could update individual components while preserving the larger data infrastructure.
Building a C2 ecosystem that evolves
Implementation of the Army’s Modular Open Systems Approach to NGC2 also makes it easier to move beyond specific suppliers and systems when they underperform or aren’t pacing evolving threats with improvements. At the 25th ID, Lockheed Martin runs what Marshall called a strict onboarding and offboarding process, evaluating each element with the Army to decide whether it is the right fit for its piece of the architecture.
That differs from traditional acquisition programs in which a single prime contractor may control much of the system and replacing a supplier can mean extensive integration work. By establishing common interfaces and services, the Army is attempting to make competition and continuous upgrades part of the architecture itself.
The ecosystem is already large. More than 60 companies have contributed to the Army’s NGC2 effort or are under analysis for it, Marshall said, including small businesses, nontraditional innovators, and commercial-technology providers. The 25th ID’s data platform is based on Raft’s Raft Data Platform. Amazon Web Services supplies Wickr Chat, a communications and collaboration tool. Rune Technologies delivered TyrOS for contested logistics.
For the Army, the larger test will be whether the approach demonstrated by the 25th ID can be extended to other formations without recreating the stovepipes NGC2 was designed to eliminate. The ongoing Lightning Surge exercises and the 4th Infantry Division’s Ivy Sting exercises at Fort Carson represent opportunities to evaluate how common data infrastructure, modular applications, and soldier-driven software development can support different operational requirements.
The stakes are particularly high in the Indo-Pacific, where formations will be separated by thousands of miles and forced to operate with intermittent comms. A shared architecture will not eliminate those constraints, but it could give commanders the ability to exploit available data, change communications equipment, and incorporate new capabilities without rebuilding the entire C2 network.

What if BMW's New i3 Is Right and Everything We Know About Designing a Modern Sedan Is Wrong?
9 photos
Photo: WheelsAge
There's something slightly awkward about the all-new BMW i3. It obviously has everything to do with its Neue Klasse design language, which to be fair does come with a suitably futuristic-looking front end, clean bumper-to-bumper surfaces, and a properly futuristic rear end.
Yet, whenever I look at it from the side, or even a front 3/4 angle, the proportions seem a little off. The hood is too short, the passenger compartment sits too far forward (also known as a cab-forward aesthetic), and it's almost like there's not enough room between the front doors and the front wheels.
I reckon much of that awkwardness comes down to what we're accustomed to seeing on a regular basis. For the better part of a century, the traditional sedan has adhered to a fairly predictable formula. It's got a relatively long hood, either a mid-cab or a cab-rearward aesthetic, and a trunk extending well beyond the rear window. Of course, we've seen a whole bunch of variations, but the basic proportions have remained consistent.
BMW spent decades perfecting this formula so that it may reflect favorably upon their products. From the E39 5er to the E46 3 Series, or even the outgoing G20 and G30 - they all have a long hood, a short front overhang and a rearward positioning of the cabin. The latter has always been fundamental to the brand's design identity , and we associate these proportions with sportiness. We don't even need to see a badge. Even a silhouette would suffice.
To me, a BMW sedan is supposed to look like a rear-wheel drive car, and I'm sure I'm not the only one who feels that way.
But there's a flip side to that argument. Throughout history, the engineers were more or less in charge of these specific proportions, as opposed to the designers. You need room at the front for a longitudinally mounted engine, especially of the six or eight-cylinder variety. Then you add the transmission, cooling, crash structures... and you eventually land on a substantial front end with a long hood.
Photo: WheelsAge Over time, these necessities became synonymous with performance and even elegance. Whereas a short hood, well, that's something you'd expect to find on a compact budget car or a minivan - something that's trying to maximize interior space so as to make up for everything else it's lacking (usually quality and/or performance).
This is why I'm singling out the new i3 . What BMW have done is that they've messed around with one of the most recognizable silhouettes in the industry. Gone are your traditional BMW sedan proportions and here comes this cab-forward experiment, with a less dominant hood and a more dominant cabin. The ratio between the front axle and the windshield is quite different than what we've come to expect from any 3 Series derivative. It'll take some getting used to, that's for sure.
But here's the thing. More recently, I've been wondering whether this reaction says more about the car itself or about the way we've been conditioned to perceive car design in general? An electric motor occupies a fraction of the space required by a combustion engine, and there's no inherent reason for the cabin to sit as far back as it traditionally sits. By moving it forward, you free up space for the occupants, and you can improve the overall package efficiency. I get all that.
And still, this is 100% a choice. Make no mistake about it. Look at the Model S , the OG EV, so to speak. Tesla could have designed it any which way, but they chose to go with a conventional premium "sedan" shape. I say "sedan" because it's technically a fastback, but the point is that it's got a long hood - like you'd expect from a combustion engine car.
Wait, haven't we seen this before? If you mean the cab-forward aesthetic, yes. Yes we have. Allow me to take you back to the 90s and to Chrysler's LH-platform sedans, the Dodge Intrepid and the Chrysler Concorde. Both these cars had their windshields pushed forward, relatively short hoods, and barely any distance between the front doors and the wheel wells. Almost no distance, actually.
Photo: WheelsAge They looked properly futuristic compared to all those boxy sedans that preceded them. Yet cab-forward design never became the universal standard. I guess people just weren't ready for it.
But now imagine someone born in 2040 (and getting their driver's license in 2058) looking back at a BMW 3 Series from 2020. The idea of dedicating such a large proportion of a sedan's overall length to the engine compartment could look peculiar to that person if future vehicles go on to abandon the long-hood aesthetic altogether.
Would that person even find the G20 elegant or good-looking? Would a long hood still communicate sportiness to us? It's an interesting thought experiment. There's no guarantee that our current understanding of what makes a sedan beautiful will endure another 50-100 years. Besides, I already told you where I think the three-box sedan is going in the long term - extinct. I think fastbacks are going to take over eventually. But that's hardly the point of this op-ed.
The point is that maybe myself, and others like me, we just don't "get" the new i3. We don't perceive it the way it's meant to be perceived. I'm willing to give it the benefit of the doubt. I still think the G50 3 Series looks better, but I can certainly change my opinion if the i3 somehow wins me over. I look forward to reviewing it for you guys as soon as possible.
I also realize that I've spent my entire life looking at cars with proportions shaped by the need to accommodate combustion engines. Maybe this is the part worth questioning. It's entirely plausible (not probable) that 20 years from now, we might look back at the second-generation i3 and see an early example of BMW establishing a new norm in terms of three-box sedan proportions.

Someone Offered $347,000 for This 2027 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X and Somehow That Still Wasn't Enough
20 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Now, before we start feeling sorry for the seller, let's crunch some numbers. This particular ZR1X Convertible packs an original sticker price of $295,000, which means the highest bidder was willing to pay $52,000 over MSRP. Unfortunately for them, the seller, a dealer out of California, had a higher number in mind.
But is $347,000 (plus a buyer's fee) a reasonable offer? I'd say so - despite the fact that we've already seen other dealers dumping their ZR1X Convertibles for three figures over sticker. So yeah, there's plenty of money to be made on these things, assuming you can find the right buyer.
I've also noticed that people have been trying to get prices to go down on the ZR1X at auction, and all it takes is one seller to bite and that pretty much shifts the market instantly, whether other sellers like it or not. Still, how much more could this car have fetched? Are we talking $360,000? Maybe $375,000? I'm genuinely not sure why you would pay such a premium at this point in time. But I guess it depends on how badly you want the car, and whether or not it's a delivery miles example.
This one here certainly is, with just 4 miles on the odometer. It also comes with a Blade Silver Metallic exterior, which I really like.
I think this is one of my favorite C8 colors, to be honest. And it works really well together with the asymmetrical Edge Red and Carbon Flash racing stripes - not to mention the carbon fiber mirror caps, a carbon fiber rear wing, tall hood spoiler, front dive planes, LED headlights and the carbon fiber accents for the power-retractable hardtop. If you like carbon fiber, there's plenty of it to go around on this car. Let's just say that.
The 20" and 21" wheels are also carbon fiber and are wrapped in Michelin rubber while housing carbon-ceramic discs and the optional Edge Red-painted calipers. The car does come with the ZTK Performance suspension courtesy of the Performance Track Package , and there's a front-axle lift system for good measure. The latter is an absolute must-have on a ZR1X, especially with such a track-focused spec. Not that you'd want to take this car out on track if you're a collector.
Photo: Bring a Trailer We can't mention the interior without discussing the asymmetrical upholstery. The left-side heated and ventilated GT2 bucket seats are trimmed in Adrenaline Red leather with black accents, while the right-side seat features Jet Black leather.
Furthermore, contrast stitching can be found throughout the cabin. Other highlights include the Stealth Interior Trim Package, a performance data and video recorder, a 14-speaker Bose Performance Series sound system, wireless charging, a head-up display, and plenty more.
As for performance, it all comes down to the mid-mounted twin-turbo 5.5-liter LT7 V8 engine, working alongside an electric motor and a 1.9-kWh battery pack. Together, they produce 1,250 horsepower and 973 lb-ft (1,320 Nm) of torque, with everything hitting all four wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic and an electronic all-wheel drive system.

Traffic congestion on U.S. highways cost the trucking industry an estimated $128.2 billion in 2024, according to a report released this week by the American Transportation Research Institute (ATRI) . It was the second-highest total the group has recorded and the third straight year the bill topped $120 billion.
What’s Related
The national total fell from a record $129.8 billion in 2023. ATRI attributed the dip to lower truck mileage during the freight slump. Truck miles fell 1.5% in 2024, while average truck speeds on the congested freight routes ATRI tracked fell from 52.09 mph to 51.84 mph.
Trucks lost a combined 1.24 billion hours to traffic in 2024. That’s the equivalent of about 452,000 truck drivers sitting idle for an entire working year, according to ATRI. The average cost came to $7,973 per registered truck.
RELATED STORIES: Ranking The Top 10 U.S. Locations For Worst Truck Traffic | The Top 10 Issues Facing the Trucking Industry in 2026
The cost of time and fuel
ATRI used truck GPS data , federal highway figures, and its own trucking cost research to estimate the cost of delays. The group updated its hourly trucking cost calculation and applied the change to past years. On that basis, the 2024 total was $4.7 billion higher than in 2022 and nearly 29% above the pre-pandemic peak of $99.5 billion in 2018.
ATRI estimated that congestion caused trucks to burn 6.66 billion gallons of diesel in 2024, costing about $25 billion. Higher trucking costs and a return of highway traffic after the pandemic have kept the congestion bill near record levels, said Jeremy Carmichael, vice president of operations at Ruan Transportation Management Systems.
“These costs can be addressed through targeted infrastructure investment in the nation’s most congested freight corridors, and a commitment at every level of government to upgrade our highways and improve supply chain efficiency,” Carmichael said.
Where costs were the highest
Texas led all states at $10.92 billion, followed by California at $10.47 billion and Florida at $10.35 billion. Together, the 10 states with the highest costs accounted for 53% of the national total.
The New York City metro area ranked first at $7.49 billion, ahead of Miami at $3.69 billion and Chicago at $3.54 billion. ATRI used 2022 as the baseline for changes in state and metro costs. Over those two years, costs rose in 73 of the 107 metro areas studied. Charleston, South Carolina, had the largest percentage increase at 20.9%, which ATRI linked to rising port freight volumes and population growth.
Truck traffic is outgrowing the interstates
Over the decade through 2024, tractor-trailer mileage on interstates grew nearly 25%, while interstate lane mileage increased 4.5%. About 57% of tractor-trailer miles in 2024 were driven on interstates.
“Investments like the Hunts Point Interstate Access Project in the Bronx are essential to improving freight mobility and supporting our region’s growth,” said Zach Miller, vice president of government affairs for the Trucking Association of New York. “We need sustained investment in infrastructure to reduce congestion and the costs it imposes on businesses and consumers.”

2027 Toyota Sienna Released with Tons of Changes, Throws More Power to the Road
29 photos
Photo: Toyota
Minivans of America, beware! The 2027 Toyota Sienna is coming for you, and this time it brings along much more than just a visual makeover and some extra creature comforts – the changes the Japanese carmaker has planned include more power from the hybrid system, more safety features, and extra technology.
Scheduled to hit Toyota dealers across the U.S. early next year, the biggest change the 2027 Sienna brings along is the new 6th-generation hybrid system. Everything about it is different from before, including the internal combustion engine, the electric motors, and the battery pack.
Built from the ground up with larger vehicles that need higher-capacity hybrid hardware in mind, the tech is centered around a 2.5-liter engine, a 124-kW electric drive motor (and also another 40-kW motor for the rear axle in all-wheel drive versions), and a 1.15 kWh lithium-ion battery.
The 6th gen delivers a combined 251 horsepower, which is up six horsepower from before. A minuscule increase, you could argue, but do keep in mind that we're talking about a people mover, not a race car. Torque levels, on the other hand, remain the same as before, 176 lb.-ft.
The new power levels allow the Sienna in front-wheel-drive configuration to accelerate from standstill to 60 mph in 7.5 seconds, something that will definitely make the kids in the back feel like they're in a fighter jet taking off from the deck of an aircraft carrier.
Photo: Toyota The engine has a fuel consumption rating, as measured by Toyota, of 39 mpg (six liters/100 km) in city driving, some three mpg better than before. The highway and combined ratings stand at 35 and 37 mpg, respectively.
Toyota revealed it has also tampered with the minivan's handling by fitting new electronic power steering components, including a new steering column and steering wheel. The steering gearbox, motor control unit (MCU), and torque sensor are also new, and they should aid the van to minimize steering effort at low speeds and increase on-center definition at highway speeds.
The Japanese also upgraded the electrical platform of the 2027 Sienna , and that allowed the deployment of the Toyota Safety Sense 4.0 suite, which makes the model the fourth to get it, following the 2026 RAV4 and 2027 Tundra and Sequoia. This solution packs upgraded sensors and hardware, and also throws in a dash cam as standard.
Another mechanical upgrade the new Sienna brings along is the electronically controlled brake system that debuted on the 2026 RAV4. Just like in that application, it is meant to maximize brake feel while also minimizing body roll.
Photo: Toyota Finally, the already very quiet cabin of the minivan has been made even more so by the addition of a new, higher-density dash silencer. Supposedly, this hardware will cut the level of noise that enters the cabin by a tiny 1.6 decibels.
For the needs of the occupants, the new Sienna is now equipped with a 12.3-inch touchscreen to handle infotainment needs, running Toyota's audio multimedia system. As a reminder, the LE grade of the previous version came with an eight-inch screen.
This tech is backed by a 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster that replaces the previous seven-inch screen on the LE and XLE models. An even bigger screen, sized at 12.9 inches, can be had when going for the optional rear seat entertainment center on the Woodland, XSE, and Platinum models.
Speaking of trim levels, the 2027 Sienna offering is a tad simpler than it used to be, as it is offered in five trim levels, namely LE, XLE, Woodland, XSE, and Platinum. As you can see, the current Limited is no longer around, as it was made redundant by the upgrades made to the XSE grade. Among them, ventilated seats for driver and right-side passenger, a heads-up display, and a panoramic view monitor, among others.
Photo: Toyota Some of the other trim levels come with their own novelties as well. The LE, for instance, is now equipped with a rear lift gate kick sensor that's offered as standard when the towing hitch is not equipped, while the rest of them all get an eight-way power-adjustable front passenger seat. A panoramic view monitor is now standard on the Woodland .
The new Sienna will be available in up to three rows of seats, and in an eight-seat configuration with a stowable middle seat. There are also second-row captain’s chairs on the table for seven-seat models.
The 2027 Sienna will continue to be assembled at the Toyota facility in Princeton, Indiana, on the Toyota Next Generation-K (TNG-K) platform. As said, the new version will hit the roads early next year, but Toyota keeps its lips tight when it comes to pricing.
As a reminder, the present-day Sienna starts at $41,320. It's likely the same color choices available now will apply to the 2027 minivan as well, with the exception of the Cypress exterior paint, which has been discontinued, and with the addition of Storm Cloud.

Google Will Place Solar-Powered AI Data Centers in Space Using the Blue Origin New Glenn Rocket
12 photos
Photo: Blue Origin
When Elon Musk decided it would be a good idea to place Internet satellites in orbit, a lot of people probably asked themselves how come they didn't think about this first. It was a brilliant thought that opened up worlds of possibilities, as Internet from space can reach any place on the planet, regardless of what's happening on the ground. And now the world seems ready for the next step.
While a number of companies (and even countries) are now following in SpaceX's footsteps and are building their own Internet satellite constellations, Google is thinking about something different. That would be the creation of AI data centers in orbit, capable of harnessing the power of the Sun to work - as a side note, SpaceX is working on something similar, they call it Starmind .
Google seems to be a bit ahead of Elon Musk's company in this respect, as it has already decided when the first AI satellite will be placed in orbit, and who will transport it there. That would be 2029, and Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, respectively.
Jeff Bezos' space company is the one that announced this week that Google will deploy to orbit, before the end of the decade, the first elements of its AI constellation, which is for now known as Project Suncatcher. The New Glenn will carry it into sun-synchronous orbit in the first quarter of 2029.
It's unclear how many of these satellites will fly on this first mission, but we do know that each of them will have the computing capacity of a data center rack. They will have the ability to harness the solar power that's abundant, continuous, and free in space, and they'll be equipped with AI chips Google likes to call Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).
There is a long road to travel before getting there, though. Google has been working on the idea for years, and only recently transformed it into something real by launching a first prototype using SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission in October 2026.
The hardware is about the size of a refrigerator, and it is equipped with four TPUs. Its purpose is to allow the technology giant to test spaceflight stress, radiation, and the thermal limits of the hardware. The mission is scheduled to last about a year and includes running a series of AI workloads like the DeepMind Gemma open model.
Come next year, Google plans to launch an additional two satellites (it's unclear who will handle this particular launch), destined to test high-speed laser communications between orbiting spacecraft – something that's crucial to making the AI data center network worthwhile.
If everything checks out, the company will move to start building the orbital network itself, probably sometime early next decade. We'll keep an eye on this story and report back once we know more.

COSCO Shipping ​​​​​​signed two logistics deals at a trade show in Shanghai on Nov. 6. One builds on its warehouse work with Western Post in Los Angeles. The other expands its work with Xiaomi in Panama, where a warehouse project has handled more than 1 million phones.
What’s Related
COSCO Shipping North America signed a memorandum of understanding with Western Post (US) LLC at the China International Import Expo. COSCO Shipping Lines Central America signed a separate agreement with Xiaomi H.K. Limited at the same event.
“Today's supply chains demand more than moving goods from one place to another. Customers need logistics partners who can connect transportation , warehousing and distribution into a seamless operation,” said Ma Jie, president of COSCO Shipping North America.
Western Post goes beyond warehousing
COSCO and Western Post began working together on warehousing in Los Angeles in 2024. Under the new agreement, they plan to better coordinate ocean shipments with warehousing and inland delivery for cross-border e-commerce customers.
Ze Kuaiyue, founder of AuGroup, said the companies would explore how to provide warehouse services for Chinese businesses expanding overseas. The agreement builds on the Los Angeles partnership by bringing the shipping and delivery legs into the work the companies already do together at the warehouse.
Xiaomi looks to expand past Panama
COSCO and Xiaomi plan to expand their work on warehouse management and order fulfillment , along with distribution across the region. They also plan to coordinate ocean and air shipments more closely with customs clearance and inland transportation. The agreement calls for exploring opportunities in North America and elsewhere in Latin America.
“Building on our successful cooperation with COSCO SHIPPING in Panama, we look forward to leveraging COSCO SHIPPING’s global network and integrated supply chain capabilities to deliver reliable and efficient logistics solutions as we expand our regional footprint,” said Liu Cong, general manager of Xiaomi Group’s international delivery department.
How COSCO handles trans-Pacific orders
At the expo, COSCO Shipping North America demonstrated how it connects the steps involved in moving an e-commerce order across the Pacific. The demonstration showed how its systems link shipping and warehousing with final-mile delivery , the leg that takes a package to the customer.
COSCO also hosted a panel on AI in logistics. Participants from C.H. Robinson , Xiaomi, and other organizations discussed where AI could help with logistics decisions and where people still need to use their judgment.

Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 20, 2026
Chile’s lithium investment pipeline has more than doubled to $10.8 billion (C$15.5 billion), accounting for most of the growth in the country’s mining project portfolio as two major developments await environmental approval.
The Chilean Copper Commission (Cochilco) has identified $111.1 billion in planned mining investment between 2026 and 2035, the highest level in 13 years. The portfolio grew 6.3% from $104.5 billion in the previous survey, with lithium contributing $6.1 billion of the $6.6-billion increase.
Both lithium developments would introduce direct lithium extraction (DLE), a technology designed to boost recovery from brine. Albemarle’s proposal would complement its existing evaporation-based operation.
GEM Mining Consulting forecasts that Argentina could overtake Chile as South America’s largest lithium producer by 2035, according to Mining.com . That outcome depends heavily on delivery of the Pozuelos–Pastos Grandes project in Argentina, the consultancy’s analysis found.
Lithium projects
Two projects undergoing environmental review account for $6.1 billion, or more than half of the country’s planned lithium investment.
The larger is Albemarle ’s (NYSE: ALB) $3.1-billion transition to DLE at the Salar de Atacama, which the company says could recover nearly twice as much lithium as its existing operation.
Novandino Litio, the public-private partnership between state-owned Codelco and SQM (NYSE: SQM), plans to spend $3 billion on Salar Futuro. The initiative aims to sustain operations at the Salar de Atacama between 2031 and 2060 by introducing new extraction technologies and reducing net brine withdrawals.
Both projects are under review by Chile’s Environmental Assessment Service. Their progress through permitting will help determine when the proposed investments can advance.
Cochilco’s acting executive vice-president, Claudia Rodríguez, presented the latest outlook at the World Copper Conference Asia in Shanghai, organized by UK consultancy CRU on Nov. 18–19.
The portfolio includes 72 projects over the coming decade, up from 59 in the previous survey. It contains “more initiatives with advanced technical and environmental definitions,” Rodríguez said in a statement, translated from Spanish.
Copper nevertheless accounts for 84.5% of planned spending, or about US$93.9 billion.
Among the projects is BHP’s (ASX, LON, NYSE: BHP) US$1.3-billion extension of Escondida’s B1 leach pad, designed to sustain annual production of 210,000 tonnes of copper cathodes.
Capstone Copper (TSX: CS; ASX: CSC) is also planning US$500 million in improvements at Mantos Blancos, extending operations to 2041 and increasing sulphide processing capacity to 9.8 million tonnes annually.
Regional pressures
Antofagasta leads Chile’s regions with US$51.5 billion in planned mining investment, representing about 46% of the national total. Copper projects account for US$45 billion of that amount, or roughly 87%.
The regional pipeline also includes proposed upgrades at Escondida, Spence and Sierra Gorda.
The Capricorn Bioceanic Corridor is intended to link Brazil, Paraguay and Argentina with northern Chile’s Pacific ports, strengthening the region’s transport connections.
Antofagasta also depends on workers from elsewhere in Chile. A Nov. 16 report by the National Statistics Institute, based on the 2024 census, found a net inflow of 27 workers from other regions for every 100 employed residents.
For Novandino, the longer-term investment would accompany a shift in management. SQM manages the venture through 2030, with Codelco due to take over in 2031 under the partners’ agreement.

GLASGOW, Scotland — Two German one-way attack drone variants passed live-fire trials this month, clearing a step toward initial deliveries and troop training before the end of the year, Germany’s military procurement office said.
Though the systems have yet to complete qualification, the German Army plans to begin equipping its armored brigade in Lithuania in 2027.
The trials, held the week of Nov. 9, tested whether Stark’s Virtus and Helsing’s HX-2 could reliably hit designated targets and whether their warheads worked as intended on impact. The Bundeswehr conducted key parts of the testing at its weapons and ammunition test center in Meppen. The procurement office announced that both systems passed but did not disclose how many shots it fired or the weapons’ success rates.
Photos attached to the statement showed both an OWE-V Virtus and an HX-2 loitering munition moments before impact into a tank.
Both systems are loitering munitions, weapons that can remain airborne over an area while searching for targets before a human operator decides whether to authorize a strike. The live-fire campaign focused on the final part of that process, from the approach to the target through the effect of the warhead, rather than certifying the systems for service.
The military noted that before loitering munitions can be used within the German Armed Forces, they must be thoroughly tested on the “interaction of the various system components.”
German lawmakers were previously skeptical of approving armed drones for the country’s military, and some arms control researchers have raised concerns about autonomous targeting in loitering munitions.
The tests follow a Feb. 25 vote by Germany’s parliamentary budget committee approving contracts worth €268 million ($294.4 million) apiece for Stark and Helsing. Options could add €1 billion to each deal, but further purchases depend on the systems proving technologically mature and lawmakers approving the spending, Defense News reported in February. The vote marked a shift that’s part of a larger rethinking of Germany’s military posture in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Germany is trying to shorten the time between signing a contract and getting the weapons to troops by allowing concurrent development, testing, qualification and preparations for use. The procurement office said it brought soldiers into testing early so their feedback could inform changes to the systems. Lawmakers attached reporting requirements to the spending plan, and cancellation clauses allow the government to walk away if a system fails qualification.
The procurement office said it expects initial deliveries this year so troops can begin training. It did not say how many weapons would arrive in that first batch. The army intends eventually to link the munitions with its reconnaissance and strike systems, with the 45th Armored Brigade in Lithuania slated to become the first major formation to receive them starting in 2027.

The gold price has hit its lowest point since September 2025. Credit: Adobe Stock Photo by monsitj.
Posted By: Colin McClelland November 20, 2026
Bets on a December U.S. rate increase helped drive gold towards $3,500 an oz. Friday, testing miners’ budgets after all-in sustaining costs rose 22% year on year in the second quarter, the steepest rise since 2013, according to the World Gold Council.
Spot gold traded at $3,576.25 per oz. at 9:59 a.m. Friday in New York, according to GoldPrice.com . Bullion had touched $3,513.54 earlier in the session, its lowest since September 2025. Traders put the odds of a quarter-point rate increase at 99%, according to CME FedWatch.
Higher Treasury yields make bonds more attractive to investors who might otherwise hold gold, which pays no interest. A stronger dollar makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.
As technology stocks fell, “bullion has become a source of cash for investors facing mounting losses elsewhere,” Ole Hansen , head of commodity strategy at Denmark’s Saxo Bank, wrote Friday.
Miners spent a record $441 (C$631) per oz. on capital to sustain output in the second quarter, up 34% from the first. The increase in that spending accounted for about 80% of the quarterly rise in all-in sustaining costs to $1,930 per oz., Oliver Blagden of London-based precious metals consultancy Metals Focus wrote in a Nov. 10 analysis published by the gold council.
Margins
The margin above those costs fell 16% from the first quarter to $2,582 per oz., leaving less cash per ounce for new projects and shareholder returns. It was still the second-highest margin Metals Focus has recorded.
Nearly all Federal Reserve policymakers expected further rate increases to curb inflation, according to minutes released Wednesday. Meanwhile, gold holdings in exchange-traded funds tracked by Bloomberg were little changed over the past month despite a roughly 10% price drop, Saxo’s Hansen said.
Barrick Mining (TSX: ABX; NYSE: B) realized $174 less for each ounce it sold in the third quarter while all-in sustaining costs rose $45 to $1,911 per oz. That narrowed the margin by $219 to $2,332 an ounce, its quarterly figures show.
Miners produced 1,071 tonnes worldwide in the third quarter, up 3% year on year and a record for that quarter, the council said in its quarterly review . New mines including Goose in Nunavut helped lift Canadian output 22%.
Goose
B2Gold (TSX: BTO; NYSE-A: BTG) sold 17,426 oz. of gold from its Goose mine in Nunavut in the second quarter , when an April fire in the crushing circuit reduced the amount of ore the mill could process. The mine sold fewer ounces than expected and incurred costs it had budgeted for the first quarter, pushing all-in sustaining costs to $6,390 per oz. sold, B2Gold said.
Goose sold 30,894 oz. in the third quarter , spreading costs over more ounces. All-in sustaining costs at the mine fell 25% to $4,816 per oz. sold, while B2Gold’s companywide average rose to $2,602 from $2,356.
The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (NYSE Arca: GDX) closed Thursday at $72 in New York, 12% weaker than the previous Friday.
Agnico
On Wednesday, Ralph Profiti, a mining analyst at U.S. investment bank Stifel, asked Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX, NYSE: AEM) whether $3,500 gold would force it to postpone projects or cut exploration.
“So, really nothing changes at $3,500 gold. I’d suggest nothing changes at $3,000 gold,” Agnico chief financial officer Jamie Porter said at the briefing in Toronto.
Agnico’s sustaining spending rose from $237 million in the second quarter to $287 million in the third, including $96 million at Detour Lake in Ontario, the company reported in October.
Canada’s largest gold producer by market cap and output expects capital spending to exceed $3.5 billion next year, including growth projects and capitalized exploration, Porter said. Its main projects remain on track, though higher drilling rates could put off some exploration.

BlueGrace Logistics announced it will change private equity hands. The managed logistics provider said middle-market investor Littlejohn & Co. will replace Warburg Pincus as its primary growth partner.
Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed. The deal is expected to close by the end of the year.
Tampa, Florida-based BlueGrace serves more than 10,000 customers out of offices in the U.S. and Mexico. The deal will include additional investment in its BlueShip platform, which has over 250,000 carriers, providing less-than-truckload, truckload, reefer and multimodal transportation services. The transaction will also help BlueGrace expand its logistics staff and account teams.
“BlueGrace is growing, and this gives us a partner who shares our long-term view to keep doing what’s working, investing in our people, in BlueShip, and in the service our customers and carriers count on,” said Bobby Harris, founder and CEO of BlueGrace Logistics, in a news release.
The company will continue to be led by the current leadership team, including Harris.
The release didn’t mention future M&A, but BlueGrace has been acquisitive over the past two years. It acquired Idaho-based 3PL Truk TMS in August. Last year, it acquired Michigan-based 3PL STB Freight Group and Florida-based broker FreightCenter .
“Warburg Pincus has been a strong partner through this stage of our growth, and I’m grateful for their support,” Harris said. “With Littlejohn’s backing, we’re building for the long run.”
Evercore is serving as financial adviser to BlueGrace, with J.P. Morgan advising Littlejohn.
Why it matters? BlueGrace’s transition to a new private equity partner and track record of acquisitions highlight robust capital availability and aggressive expansion within the 3PL sector. Additionally, ongoing investments in proprietary platforms like BlueShip emphasize the need for scaled digital capabilities to remain competitive.

A view of the Pitarillo project area. Credit: Endeavour Silver via Facebook.
Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 20, 2026
Endeavour Silver (TSX: EDR; NYSE: EXK) puts the initial cost of building its Pitarrilla project in Mexico at $585 million (C$837.5 million) — just as the metal has slipped below the $50 per oz. that the company assumed in its feasibility study .
Spot silver traded at $42.58 an oz. early Friday. At $40 silver, the project’s after-tax net present value would fall to $423 million from $736 million at $50, using a 5% discount rate. The corresponding internal rate of return would drop to 12% from 16.4%, the Vancouver-based producer said in study results released after markets closed Thursday.
Pitarrilla “adds an advanced stage, long life growth asset, capable of being funded internally with upside opportunities ahead,” TD Securities mining analyst Wayne Lam said in a note late Thursday. “We view the project further positioning Endeavour favourably within the silver space in transforming the portfolio, complementing the brand new Terronera and recently acquired Kolpa mines.”
Located about 950 km northwest of Mexico City and accessible by regional roads, the planned underground operation would produce an average of 5.4 million oz. of silver, 13,000 tonnes of lead and 29,000 tonnes of zinc annually over 18 years. Revenue from lead and zinc would help bring mine-site all-in sustaining costs to $15.06 per payable silver ounce, Endeavour estimates.
Self-financed
Endeavour expects to fund the majority of construction of Pitarrilla through a combination of cash on hand and cash flow from its operating mines. It ended September with $287.9 million in cash, about half the estimated construction cost. The spending would be spread over a 30-month construction period.
Pitarrilla has an estimated break-even silver price of less than $30 per oz., Endeavour said Thursday. The company realized $62.42 per oz. on third-quarter silver sales, it said last week in its third- quarter report.
National Bank analyst Alex Terentiew agrees with Endeavour’s assessment. Even at current spot metal prices of $3,600 per oz. gold and $42.50 silver, he predicts that Endeavour will keep a cash balance of at least $200 million over the development period, “leaving it with more than sufficient liquidity to advance the project on our schedule.”
Improved visibility
Endeavour’s new analysis replaces a 2009 underground prefeasibility study and a 2012 open-pit feasibility study with a current underground development plan, “materially improving visibility on capital, production and cash flow,” Terentiew said.
“In essence, today’s updated mine plan showcases a more targeted underground sulphide development strategy, representing a reduced operational footprint and a shift from the open-pit concept outlined in the 2012 feasibility study prepared by the previous operator,” CIBC mining analyst Cosmos Chiu said in a note.
Endeavour has approvals for underground development, mining and water use. It still needs a permit for its proposed dry-stack tailings site and other approvals and amendments, and its board has yet to make a construction decision.
Terentiew models first production in 2030, assuming that the tailings permit arrives in 2027 and construction starts in late 2027 or early 2028.
Endeavour shares dropped 1.8% to C$8.57 Friday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$2.5 billion ($1.7 billion). The stock has traded between C$8.70 and C$20.70 in the past year.

Licensed from Kelun-Biotech, Merck’s TROP2-targeting antibody drug conjugate sac-TMT improved overall survival in advanced gastroesophageal cancer while missing on two secondary endpoints.
Merck’s TROP2 antibody drug conjugate sac-TMT improved overall survival in a late-stage gastroesophageal cancer trial—the second Phase 3 success in its global program of 18 late-stage studies.
The study did miss on two secondary endpoints, however: progression free survival (PFS) and objective response rate (ORR), according to a Friday press release .
Neither Merck nor Kelun-Biotech, the China startup that discovered sacituzumab tirumotecan (sac-TMT), shared data behind the win.
The topline readout comes from TroFuse-015 , which recruited 473 patients with advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma who have received two or more previous lines of systemic therapy. The study met its main goal of significantly improving overall survival (OS) when compared to treatment of a physician’s choice (TPC).
The results were generally consistent across subgroups regardless of TROP2 expression status, according to Merck. The Kelun-shared antibody drug conjugate (ADC) is designed to target TROP2 , a cell-surface protein overexpressed in several cancers.
Sac-TMT failed to significantly improve PFS and ORR, though the latter wasn’t formally tested under the prespecified analysis plan, according to Merck.
“While TroFuse-015 did not meet the secondary endpoint of PFS, and the nominal benefit in ORR was not formally tested, it’s not unheard of in oncology trials to see this dynamic (typically with immunotherapies) and OS remains the gold standard in these settings,” RBC Capital Markets wrote in a Friday morning note to investors.
Safety findings were consistent with previous studies, with no new safety signals observed. The Big Pharma plans on sharing the data with regulatory authorities and at an upcoming medical conference, according to Merck’s announcement.
Sac-TMT is currently approved in four indications in China and is under FDA priority review for previously treated endometrial cancer, with a decision expected by June 2027. In the U.S., the asset secured a Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher—an FDA pilot program designed to speed up reviews for products that aligned with certain national priorities. However, the program, which was launched under former FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, is now reportedly defunct .

In advance of a Senate vote on Heidi Overton as the next FDA commissioner, the agency has shelved the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher program introduced by former leader Marty Makary, Reuters reported Thursday.

“Sac-TMT is the first TROP2 ADC to improve OS in a global Phase 3 study in advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma compared to TPC, demonstrating its potential in a particularly challenging disease setting,” Marjorie Green, senior vice president and head of oncology, global clinical development at Merck Research Laboratories, said in the release. “There is a tremendous unmet need for therapies that can improve survival for these patients.”
Friday’s results follow the positive October readout for TroFuse-005 , which found that sac-TMT slashed the risk of death by 32% in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer compared to chemotherapy.
The TroFuse program consists of 18 ongoing Phase 3 studies across numerous tumor types, including endometrial, bladder, breast, cervical, gastric and ovarian cancers. Fourteen of those trials are pursuing first-in-class opportunities, including TroFuse-015.
Beyond the global TroFuse program, sac-TMT is also being tested in lung cancer, succeeding this summer in a late-stage study for first-line PD-L1-positive non-small cell lung cancer.
The ADC is situated to serve as a “meaningful part of the Keytruda solution,” BMO analysts wrote in a September report, referring to Merck’s PD-1 blockbuster that faces exclusivity losses at the end of 2028, putting $33 billion in revenue at risk.
BMO analysts have been bullish on Merck’s revenue-replacement plan and have projected peak sales of $4.3 billion for sac-TMT.
Merck joined in on development of the asset in May 2022, offering Kelun-Biotech up to $1.36 billion in biobucks to secure certain rights, according to a release translated from Chinese. Later that year, the pharma came back for more from Kelun-Biotech, offering up to $9.3 billion for seven investigational ADCs.

Volkswagen revealed the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept, an electric pocket rocket with a massive rear wing and 362 horsepower.
Will Volkswagen bring the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport to life?
We knew Volkswagen was cooking something “really spicy” up after teasing the new GTI hot hatch earlier this week.
Volkswagen launched the first-generation Golf GTI in 1976, which essentially defined the hot hatch. To celebrate the brand’s legendary performance badge, a signature of its sporty, practical hatchbacks, VW is entering a new era with its first fully electric GTI.
The GTI has been “one of Volkswagen’s great success stories for 50 years,” Volkswagen’s technical development boss, Kai Grünitz, said.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
After opening pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, the brand’s first EV to wear the badge, Volkswagen introduced the Clubsport Concept, a souped-up two-door electric pocket rocket.
The new ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept shows “how much more potential there is in the electric GTI world,” according to Grünitz.
It’s based on the production ID. Polo GTI uses the same MEB+ platform, but VW reengineered it with a larger electric motor to pump out more power.
The Clubsport is powered by a 362 hp (270 kW) front-mounted electric motor (APP550) that’s typically used in the rear of VW’s larger EVs, like the ID. Tiguan and the ID.7. That’s up considerably from the 233 hp (166 kW) and 213 lb-ft of torque of the standard ID. Polo GTI offers.
Thomas Schmall, CEO of Volkswagen Group Components, said the APP550 motor is “one of the most efficient electric drives in its class.”
Thanks to an electronically controlled front differential lock (VAQ), Volkswagen said, the Clubsport version can sprint from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in 4.7 seconds, beating the standard ID. Polo GTI by a full two seconds (6.8 seconds).
Volkswagen also fine-tuned the adaptive chassis control (DCC) to make it racetrack-ready and added new ceramic brakes to help slow it down.
The Clubsport version uses the same 52 kW NMC battery as the ID. Polo GTI, which can provide up to 389 hp (290 kW), Volkswagen said, enabling a top speed of 149 mph (240 km/h).
On the exterior, the Clubsport is a two-door model rather than a four-door. It’s 100 mm longer than the standard ID. Polo GTI, with each wing flared an additional 50 mm. It also gets a large motorsport splitter up front, a wider rear end, a new diffuser, and a massive carbon-fiber rear wing.
Inside, the cabin is tailored to the racetrack with a minimalist, stripped-down, two-seater layout. As such, there’s no infotainment system, just a center display to switch between drive modes.
The dash panel, side trims, and other interior elements feature dark ArtVelours microfibre with red topstitching, reinforcing the racetrack-ready interior.
Following the ID. Polo GTI, new ID.3 GTI, and Golf GTI Edition 50, the new ID. Polo Clubsport is the fourth model to debut this year under the performance badge.
Volkswagen opened pre-orders for the ID. Polo GTI last month, starting at 39,995 euros (about $45,000). In early 2027, Volkswagen will open orders for the ID.3 GTI , the second EV to wear the badge, and its first rear-wheel-drive (RWD) GTI.

Volkswagen didn’t confirm plans to launch a production version, but don’t expect it to reach the States.

Groundtruth, a startup developed through J.B. Hunt Transport Services’ venture-building partnership with Vantora, launched an artificial intelligence platform designed to automate freight billing validation and reduce invoice discrepancies across the transportation industry, the companies announced on Monday, Nov. 16.
Founded in 2024, Groundtruth is a Nashville-based startup with fewer than 50 employees led by CEO Alex Rustioni. The company is an independent business spun out of the venture studio operated by J.B. Hunt and Vantora, formerly UP.Labs . J.B. Hunt has served as a collaborative design partner for the past two years, while Groundtruth received funding from UP.Partners, according to a company spokesperson.
The platform is designed to reconcile information spread across different systems, including commercial agreements, shipment records, emails and operational documents. It is aimed at carriers, freight brokers and freight forwarders.
The launch comes as transportation companies continue to work through the back-office challenges associated with manual invoice processing. A December 2025 survey FreightWaves conducted with OTR Solutions found that 54% of freight brokerages described their accounts payable processes as mostly automated, but only 2% reported full automation. On the accounts receivable side, just 2% reported full automation, while 43% said their processes remained partially automated with numerous manual steps.
Invoice discrepancies are also a concern for shippers. A 2026 survey of less-than-truckload shipping professionals conducted by MyCarrier, a provider of LTL shipping software, and research firm Mastio & Company found that 67% of respondents identified disputing carrier overcharges as the most difficult or time-consuming part of their freight audit and payment process. Nearly 20% said manually comparing freight bills with bills of lading was their biggest challenge.
Groundtruth is intended to address the validation process before an invoice reaches a customer, rather than focusing on payment processing itself. The platform brings together information from transportation and finance systems, contracts and customer communications to check whether an invoice reflects the agreed terms.
Fuel surcharges are one example of the charges that require verification. Carriers typically calculate them using a contractually agreed surcharge schedule tied to the U.S. Department of Energy’s weekly average diesel price. Applying the wrong weekly price or an incorrect surcharge schedule can result in a billing discrepancy.
“When it finds an exception, it shows the customer experience team the evidence behind it. A person with context on that customer’s rates and agreements can then review it and decide whether to make a correction,” Rustioni said.
Groundtruth is close to 100% deployed across J.B. Hunt’s internal departments and is already being used daily.
The platform is also commercially available to other carriers, brokers and freight forwarders, though the company did not identify any external customers or disclose how many invoices it has processed.
Groundtruth uses a cost-to-serve pricing model, charging customers a few dollars for each invoice the platform impacts, according to a company spokesperson. The company said the model delivers a fourfold to sixfold return for customers but did not provide supporting calculations or disclose how many invoices it has processed.
Groundtruth is the second startup announced through J.B. Hunt’s partnership with Vantora, The first, Overroute , launched in July with an AI-powered freight execution platform. Billing was among the problems J.B. Hunt and Vantora weighed early on, including reducing billing complexity, before they chose load execution for Overroute.
The partnership is focused on developing startups to address operational challenges in transportation and other essential industries. Groundtruth’s launch extends that effort into freight finance and back-office operations.
Why this matters:
Freight billing errors and manual invoice reconciliation can create administrative costs, delay payments and lead to disputes between carriers, brokers and shippers. As transportation companies look to automate back-office operations, tools that validate charges against contracts, shipment records and fuel surcharge schedules could reduce manual work and improve billing accuracy.

Italy’s transport ministry has granted provisional approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” in Europe. Italy becomes the 12th European country to allow the system, and the first of the EU’s big markets.
It also didn’t wait for Brussels. The EU committee that decides on bloc-wide recognition isn’t expected to vote until December at the earliest.
Deputy Prime Minister and Transport Minister Matteo Salvini announced the decision on X on Friday. He wrote that the ministry (MIT) gave the green light after a “thorough technical feasibility check,” and that Italy is getting ahead of the EU recognition process, which he described as “still being defined.”
Tesla Europe followed with a one-liner, “Now approved in Italy, rollout begins soon,” and a video of one of its cars driving itself through Rome. There’s no firm rollout date yet.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
It’s still a Level 2 driver-assist system. It can steer, brake, accelerate, and handle intersections and lane changes, but the driver has to supervise at all times and stays fully responsible for the car.
How Italy got here
The Dutch vehicle authority RDW was first, approving FSD Supervised on April 10 under Article 39 of the EU type-approval regulation. Other member states can then recognize that approval nationally, one by one.
Ten did before Italy: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. Those are mostly small markets. Together with the Netherlands, they add up to about 70 million people, or roughly 15% of the EU’s population.
Italy alone has about 59 million people, so Friday’s decision nearly doubles the share of Europeans who can legally use the system, to close to 30%.
Rome’s position moved fast. In April, Senator Carlo Calenda formally asked Salvini’s ministry to prioritize the approval. On October 29, Salvini posted that he’d had a “very positive and constructive” call with Elon Musk and that Italy supported a “swift EU approval,” which read at the time as backing for an EU-level decision, not a national one. Three weeks later, Italy went national.
A lot changed in between. Tesla dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name in Europe after Germany’s Transport Ministry called it misleading, and cut the maximum speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit. Then on November 16, the RDW approved stricter driver monitoring , including hands on the wheel above 130 km/h. That’s the version Italy is approving.
The December math gets easier
The EU’s Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) pushed the Tesla vote to December after holding only discussions in October. Bloc-wide approval needs a qualified majority: at least 15 of 27 member states, representing at least 65% of the EU population.
Germany said in October it would back approval after Tesla agreed to the rename and the speed cap. If it follows through, Germany and the 12 approving countries would cover roughly 47% of the EU’s population.
That’s progress for Tesla, but it’s not 65%. France refused a national approval in July, and Spain hasn’t recognized the Dutch approval. Tesla needs at least one of them, plus most of the remaining holdouts.

EICMA 2026 • Honda Has a Taste of the e-MTB World with the RN0 Motor-Assisted Bicycle
General Motors Canada Ending Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Production at Oshawa
7 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
Oshawa Assembly will drop the Silverado 1500 by the end of December 2026. The Ontario facility will continue building heavy-duty pickups, though, starting with the 2027 model year Silverado HD. Later on, the Canadian plant will take on the next-generation Chevrolet Silverado HD and its GMC-branded sibling.
General Motors Canada spokesperson Ariane Souza Pereira clarified to Automotive News that production will continue on two shifts, including for the complex transitions to the redesigned Silverado HD and Sierra HD. The Detroit-based automaker will spend approximately CAD 500 million by 2030 on manufacturing upgrades and the next-generation HD truck program.
Total investments in the facility have reached CAD 1.5 billion since 2020. Part of the plant will also continue producing aftermarket components through stamping and subassembly work. Looking at the bigger picture, the loss of the Silverado 1500 does leave a sizable hole to fill.
Oshawa Assembly produced 70,551 vehicles during the first nine months of 2026, down from 95,041 over the same period last year. Said 26 percent nosedive can also be explained by GM's elimination of the third shift in January 2026, which affected 700 workers. Once next-gen production starts, the facility is expected to output in the ballpark of 100,000 Silverado HDs and Sierra HDs annually.
That would be just around half the plant's capacity, but remember that eventual output will depend on consumer demand across North America. Tariffs will play a role as well, and hopefully, the US-Canada tariff situation will be resolved after the 120th Congress convenes in January 2027 with Dems in control of the House and the Senate.
Photo: GM GM hasn't provided a debut date for the next-gen trucks, but Sam Fiorani of AutoForecast Solutions is betting that both models will start production at Oshawa in the earliest part of 2029. Considering that General Motors already replaced the L5P engine with the 8.3-liter Duramax, the next generation is likely going to steal customers from both the Ford Super Duty and Ram's HD line of workhorses.
From 2027, the Silverado 1500 will use plants in the United States and Mexico. Those factories are Fort Wayne Assembly in Indiana, the Orion Township facility in Michigan, and Silao Assembly in Guanajuato. The latter had the largest output in 2025 among the three, operating at full capacity to assemble more than 300,000 examples of the Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500.
Fort Wayne Assembly isn't far behind in terms of annual capacity. Orion, meanwhile, was initially supposed to build electric trucks. The production schedule was pushed back time and time again, with General Motors eventually announcing that internal combustion trucks would be produced there from 2027. Based on reliable info, Orion Assembly will start churning out half-ton pickups in the second quarter of 2027.
For Oshawa Assembly , its future depends on how two heavy-duty trucks compete in a segment dominated by the Detroit Big Three. The Ford Motor Company leads the segment as of November 2026, boasting 40,000 pounds (18,144 kilograms) of max gooseneck towing capacity and 7,900 (3,583) of max payload.

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern have urged the Surface Transportation Board to continue reviewing their proposed merger, pushing back against Canadian Pacific Kansas City’s request to terminate the proceeding as four rail labor organizations endorsed the transaction.
The proposed combination would create what the companies describe as the nation’s first single-line, seamless coast-to-coast railroad. Its review has drawn competing arguments over potential freight growth, employment protections, customer choice and whether stakeholders can voice objections without fear of retaliation.
A flurry of filings marked the Nov. 19 deadline for public comments.
In their response to CPKC (NYSE: CP ), Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP ) and Norfolk Southern (NYSE: NSC ) said they support a full, transparent and rigorous regulatory review and encourage stakeholders to make their views known to the STB.
Reiterating comments he made earlier to FreightWaves, UP issued its first public statement regarding remarks by Chief Executive Jim Vena at a shippers conference threatening rate hikes for shippers who didn’t support the merger.
“I do use humor in my presentations to keep the audience engaged, including in my presentation at the conference of the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers this past March,” Vena said. “I know what I said and regret the inference.”
Vena said the speech lasted more than 50 minutes and that he attempted humor near its conclusion.
“I apologize to anyone who misunderstood my statement,” he said.
Four labor organizations support merger
Separately, the SMART Transportation Division, the National Conference of Firemen and Oilers, the International Brotherhood of Boilermakers and SMART’s Mechanical Division submitted joint comments urging the STB to approve the merger.
Each organization has secured a “Jobs for Life” agreement with Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The agreements provide career-long employment commitments for covered workers, subject to their respective terms, and depend on approval and completion of the transaction.
“For generations, railroaders have been asked to carry the uncertainty while somebody else makes the decisions,” SMART-TD President Jeremy Ferguson said. “We went to the bargaining table and secured binding commitments to our members’ futures.”
For covered SMART-TD members, the protections include safeguards against involuntary furlough in their crafts, under their collective bargaining agreements and within their current seniority districts. The other organizations negotiated protections tailored to the workers they represent.
The coalition urged regulators to approve the transaction with the employment commitments honored in full, effective safety and service oversight, and continued labor involvement during implementation.
The labor organizations argue that a more connected network, fewer interchange delays and more dependable service could help railroads compete for freight now moving by truck.
Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern estimate that the combined network could shift approximately 2.1 million truckloads from highways to rail annually.
The unions contend that winning that freight would generate more railroad work while potentially reducing highway congestion and heavy-truck traffic.
“Every load we win back to rail is an opportunity for railroaders to show what we do best,” said Michael Pistone, president of the National Conference of Firemen and Oilers. “America needs a supply chain that can carry more freight safely and reliably.”
Chemical industry raises retaliation concerns
The American Chemistry Council raised a different concern, saying the application’s size and the review standards are not the only factors distinguishing the proceeding.
“This merger application differs from many that have come before it — not only because of its magnitude and the new standards of review, but also because it is being considered under a dark cloud amid concerns about potential retaliation against those who speak out,” the council said.
CN seeks competitive-access conditions
Canadian National (NYSE: CNI ) has filed proposed conditions with the STB aimed at preserving customer options and expanding its access in several Midwest markets. The proposals build on a framework negotiated with Union Pacific.
CN’s requested conditions focus on four areas:
Kansas City: Acquiring Union Pacific’s Kansas City–St. Louis line and securing access to Neff Yard.
St. Louis and East St. Louis: Improving connectivity and rail access, including shorter routes for certain shipments.
Des Moines and Avon, Iowa: Preserving access to at least two Class I railroads for affected customers.
Illinois: Protecting existing rail competition and customer choice.
In their July announcement, CN and Union Pacific said they had signed a binding memorandum of understanding covering competitive access, terminal railroad ownership and expanded Midwest operating rights. The agreement is contingent on STB approval and completion of the merger; CN also agreed not to oppose the transaction.
That framework includes CN acquiring Norfolk Southern’s interests in the Kansas City Terminal Railway and Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis, along with new access rights in the Midwest and use of Union Pacific’s Neff Yard.
The STB is expected render a decision on the merger in 2027.
Why it matters: The proposed merger if approved is likely to reshape North American logistics, but questions remain as to whether a coast-to-coast network can deliver the service improvements and freight growth its proponents project.
